results.fetch_note: RESOLVED, no longer a fetch failure. fetch.get() direct 403/blocked, but the Wayback id_ snapshot 20260227021742 returned the underlying PDF and extracted cleanly: 21 pages, 42,407 characters, full document read. Full-text search for evaluator names returned only unnamed generics — 'external subject matter experts' (p.2.1.1), 'external experts from various disciplines' (2.1.2), 'involving external experts when appropriate' (cyber red teaming), and footnote 7 'numerous experts — including third parties where appropriate'. Not one organisation is named anywhere in the document (only Meta, Llama and Meta's own CyberSecEval appear as proper nouns). DATE UNRESOLVED: the v1.1 PDF carries no publication or revision date on any page; the only date-bearing text is 'the Frontier AI Safety Commitments, which Meta signed in May 2024'. The ledger's 2025-02-03 is the release date of v1.0, not of this v1.1 revision, so it cannot be carried over. Left blank per the DATES rule rather than invented; WebSearch was unavailable (session search budget exhausted) to date v1.1 externally.

results.title: Llama Prompt Guard 2 Model Card
results.rule_cited: §1 (company-published, no external evaluator named as contributing findings). Note this item does NOT fail the Frontier-Model Rule — Llama Prompt Guard 2 86M/22M are named safety classifiers from a frontier developer, which the rule expressly counts — and it does contain measured results (AUC .998, Recall@1%FPR 97.5%, AgentDojo APR 81.2%). It is dropped solely and squarely on the §1 carve-out failing: every evaluation reported is Meta's own ('we used a private benchmark', 'we assessed').
